parsed.attack: The recipient of the claimed loop is a family-law practitioner, and they will not recommend a parent-generated evidence tool: a self-compiled log is impeachable, opposing counsel attacks it line by line, the attorney carries the downside if it backfires in a hearing, and the safe answer they already have is 'use the app the court ordered'. Even with adoption the cycle time is an intake - a practitioner takes on a handful of new custody clients a month and sees each every four to eight weeks - so the fastest possible turn is months, which cannot compound at any coefficient. The idea's own kill criterion, fewer than 10 of the first 100 payers arriving by referral, concedes the channel may simply not exist.
parsed.strongest_defence: The referral need not come from the lawyer at all: r/Divorce and r/CoParenting have hundreds of thousands of members openly trading documentation tactics, and a parent who has just been told by their solicitor to 'keep a log' installs the same day.
parsed.verdict_reason: The professional channel is gated by liability and a months-long consultation cycle, but litigating parents congregate in free forums the founder can work by hand.
